17: 
18: The primary account key is always the user's **verified email**. Signing in with any allowlisted
19: gatekeeper that yields the same verified email resolves to the same account — its `UserDurableObject`
20: is addressed by `idFromName(email)` (the same scheme as Cloudflare Access). Each gatekeeper must only
21: return an email the provider has verified (Google `email_verified`, a GitHub primary+verified email,
22: the Cloudflare account email); otherwise it returns null and can't be used to sign in.
23: 
24: ## Incremental scopes
25: 
26: Sign-in requests only the **minimal scopes** needed to verify the user's email (e.g. GitHub
27: `read:user user:email`, Google `openid email profile`, Cloudflare `offline_access user-details.read`),
28: and the gatekeeper grant created for login is **transient** — it self-destructs shortly after the
29: email is read, so signing in never leaves a broad authorization lying around. The fuller capability
30: scopes (repos, Gmail/Docs, AI Gateway billing) are requested only later, when the user explicitly
31: **connects the gatekeeper** (`connectAccount(vendorId)` with the default `scopes: "full"`), which is
32: what persists a usable connected account. `GatekeeperVendor.connectAccount` takes
33: `{ scopes: "auth" | "full" }` to choose between the two.
34: 
35: ## Sign-in flow
36: 
37: 1. The client calls `PublicApi.startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId)`. The backend creates a short-lived
38:    `PendingLogin` DO, hands the gatekeeper a `LoginConnectCallbackImpl`, and returns the gatekeeper's
39:    OAuth `url` plus an `attempt` stub (a capability wrapping the `PendingLogin` DO — no login id is
40:    exposed to the client).
41: 2. The client opens `url` in a pop-up (the gatekeeper's self-closing OAuth window) and calls
42:    `attempt.wait()`, which blocks on the `PendingLogin` DO.
43: 3. When the gatekeeper finishes, it calls `complete(user)`. The callback reads
44:    `user.getAuthenticatedEmail()`, resolves/creates the email-keyed `UserDurableObject`, mints a
45:    session, and delivers the `"<email>:<secret>"` token to the `PendingLogin` DO — which resolves the
46:    awaiting RPC.
47: 4. The client stores the token and authenticates as usual.
48: 
49: Sign-in does **not** persist a connected account: the minimal-scope grant is only used to read the
50: email and is then discarded by the gatekeeper. To use a gatekeeper's capabilities (repos, Gmail/Docs)
51: or Cloudflare AI Gateway billing, the user explicitly **connects** it afterward (which requests the
52: full scopes and persists the connection).
53: 
54: ## Configuration
55: 
56: ```
57: PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-host
58: AUTH_GATEKEEPERS=cloudflare,google,github   # which gatekeepers may sign users in (order = button order)
59: 
60: # Optional: gatekeeper sign-in only (hide username/password).
61: DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=true
62: ```

65: OAuth app with its own redirect URI:
66: 
67: - Google: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/google/oauth`
68: - GitHub: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/github/oauth`
69: - Cloudflare: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/cloudflare/oauth`

73: 
74: ## Storage / bindings
75: 
76: - `PendingLogin` (DO) — short-lived bridge between a gatekeeper login pop-up and the waiting browser,
77:   reached via `ctx.exports` (no explicit binding). Holds no durable storage: the in-flight
78:   `attempt.wait()` keeps it alive, and it's evicted once the login completes or the client disposes
79:   the `attempt` stub.

85: ├── config.ts         # AUTH_GATEKEEPERS allowlist; password-auth toggle

# Sign-in via authentication gatekeepers

Sign-in is provided by **authentication gatekeepers** — gatekeepers that advertise `providesAuth`
and can return a provider-verified email. Each such gatekeeper uses a single OAuth app for both
sign-in and (when the user later connects it) its capabilities, so there's only one OAuth app per
provider — no separate "login" vs. "gatekeeper" apps.

It's an optional, **additive** feature: for each allowlisted, auth-capable gatekeeper a "Continue
with …" button appears **alongside** the normal username/password form. Off by default — with an
empty allowlist the Workshop behaves as before (username/password, or Cloudflare Access).

The deployment opts gatekeepers into sign-in via the `AUTH_GATEKEEPERS` allowlist (comma-separated
vendor ids). Set `DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=true` to hide username/password and offer gatekeeper sign-in
only (ignored unless the allowlist is non-empty, to avoid locking everyone out).

## Identity: keyed by verified email

The primary account key is always the user's **verified email**. Signing in with any allowlisted
gatekeeper that yields the same verified email resolves to the same account — its `UserDurableObject`
is addressed by `idFromName(email)` (the same scheme as Cloudflare Access). Each gatekeeper must only
return an email the provider has verified (Google `email_verified`, a GitHub primary+verified email,
the Cloudflare account email); otherwise it returns null and can't be used to sign in.

## Incremental scopes

Sign-in requests only the **minimal scopes** needed to verify the user's email (e.g. GitHub
`read:user user:email`, Google `openid email profile`, Cloudflare `offline_access user-details.read`),
and the gatekeeper grant created for login is **transient** — it self-destructs shortly after the
email is read, so signing in never leaves a broad authorization lying around. The fuller capability
scopes (repos, Gmail/Docs, AI Gateway billing) are requested only later, when the user explicitly
**connects the gatekeeper** (`connectAccount(vendorId)` with the default `scopes: "full"`), which is
what persists a usable connected account. `GatekeeperVendor.connectAccount` takes
`{ scopes: "auth" | "full" }` to choose between the two.

## Sign-in flow

1. The client calls `PublicApi.startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId)`. The backend creates a short-lived
   `PendingLogin` DO, hands the gatekeeper a `LoginConnectCallbackImpl`, and returns the gatekeeper's
   OAuth `url` plus an `attempt` stub (a capability wrapping the `PendingLogin` DO — no login id is
   exposed to the client).
2. The client opens `url` in a pop-up (the gatekeeper's self-closing OAuth window) and calls
   `attempt.wait()`, which blocks on the `PendingLogin` DO.
3. When the gatekeeper finishes, it calls `complete(user)`. The callback reads
   `user.getAuthenticatedEmail()`, resolves/creates the email-keyed `UserDurableObject`, mints a
   session, and delivers the `"<email>:<secret>"` token to the `PendingLogin` DO — which resolves the
   awaiting RPC.
4. The client stores the token and authenticates as usual.

Sign-in does **not** persist a connected account: the minimal-scope grant is only used to read the
email and is then discarded by the gatekeeper. To use a gatekeeper's capabilities (repos, Gmail/Docs)
or Cloudflare AI Gateway billing, the user explicitly **connects** it afterward (which requests the
full scopes and persists the connection).

## Configuration

```
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-host
AUTH_GATEKEEPERS=cloudflare,google,github   # which gatekeepers may sign users in (order = button order)

# Optional: gatekeeper sign-in only (hide username/password).
DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=true
```

OAuth app credentials live on the **gatekeeper Workers**, not the backend. Register each gatekeeper's
OAuth app with its own redirect URI:

- Google: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/google/oauth`
- GitHub: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/github/oauth`
- Cloudflare: `${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/gatekeeper/cloudflare/oauth`

In local dev, `run-dev-server.ts` seeds each gatekeeper's `CLIENT_ID`/`CLIENT_SECRET` from
`GOOGLE_*` / `GITHUB_*` / `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_*` shell vars.

## Storage / bindings

- `PendingLogin` (DO) — short-lived bridge between a gatekeeper login pop-up and the waiting browser,
  reached via `ctx.exports` (no explicit binding). Holds no durable storage: the in-flight
  `attempt.wait()` keeps it alive, and it's evicted once the login completes or the client disposes
  the `attempt` stub.

## Code layout

```
auth/
├── config.ts         # AUTH_GATEKEEPERS allowlist; password-auth toggle
├── auth-vendors.ts    # GATEKEEPER_<NAME> binding lookup helpers
└── login-flow.ts      # PendingLogin DO + LoginConnectCallbackImpl
```

Client-side: `ServerConfigContext` exposes `authVendors` and `passwordAuthEnabled`;
`components/auth/OAuthButtons` renders the sign-in options (pop-up + `attempt.wait()`).

1: # Integration testing
2: 
3: This is how the integration test suites work, and why they are shaped the way they are.
4: 
5: There are two kinds of suite:
6: 
7: | | this repo's `packages/integration-tests` | a consumer repo's per-vendor suite |
8: |---|---|---|
9: | Runs | `pnpm test` (part of CI's normal test job) | its own CI step |
10: | Gatekeeper | a fixture Worker whose verification outcome the tests set | a real vendor gatekeeper, unmodified |
11: | Covers | the overseer's observer logic | a genuinely expired credential, end to end |
12: | Owns | the harness, interceptor, and RPC client | that vendor's handlers and token minting |
13: 
14: A consumer repo is one that vendors this repo as a `public/` submodule and consumes the toolkit as a
15: workspace dependency (`public/packages/integration-tests` in its `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).
16: 
17: No such suite lives in this repo, and nothing here depends on one existing. The second column is
18: described anyway because it is what the toolkit is parameterised *for*: the harness takes a list of
19: gatekeepers and the interceptor takes pluggable handler modules precisely so a suite can be added
20: outside this repo without forking either. Where this doc describes a per-vendor suite, take it as the
21: worked example of that shape — one gatekeeper run unmodified against its vendor's mocked endpoints —
22: rather than as something you will find here.
23: 
24: ## What these tests are
25:

# Integration testing

This is how the integration test suites work, and why they are shaped the way they are.

There are two kinds of suite:

| | this repo's `packages/integration-tests` | a consumer repo's per-vendor suite |
|---|---|---|
| Runs | `pnpm test` (part of CI's normal test job) | its own CI step |
| Gatekeeper | a fixture Worker whose verification outcome the tests set | a real vendor gatekeeper, unmodified |
| Covers | the overseer's observer logic | a genuinely expired credential, end to end |
| Owns | the harness, interceptor, and RPC client | that vendor's handlers and token minting |

A consumer repo is one that vendors this repo as a `public/` submodule and consumes the toolkit as a
workspace dependency (`public/packages/integration-tests` in its `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).

No such suite lives in this repo, and nothing here depends on one existing. The second column is
described anyway because it is what the toolkit is parameterised *for*: the harness takes a list of
gatekeepers and the interceptor takes pluggable handler modules precisely so a suite can be added
outside this repo without forking either. Where this doc describes a per-vendor suite, take it as the
worked example of that shape — one gatekeeper run unmodified against its vendor's mocked endpoints —
rather than as something you will find here.

## What these tests are

`wrangler`'s [`createTestHarness()`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-07-21-integration-test-harness/)
boots `workshop-backend` and one or more gatekeepers as **real Workers in workerd**, with their
checked-in `wrangler.jsonc` patched in memory. Tests speak Cap'n Web over a WebSocket to `/api` — the
same transport the browser uses — and serve an `ObserverConfigCallback` the overseer calls back into.

Nothing is stubbed except outbound HTTP. The consequence worth internalising: **the code under test is
in another process.** Most of what follows falls out of that.

## Findings that shape the design

### Fake timers cannot work here

`vi.useFakeTimers()` patches the test process's clock. The code under test reads workerd's clock, out
of process, so a faked clock is invisible to it. `isTokenExpired()`'s 30-second skew is inside
`gatekeeper-shared` and evaluated inside the Worker.

(Fake timers *do* work for in-isolate unit tests under `vitest-pool-workers`, where the test runs
inside the same isolate)

### A fixture gatekeeper, not a real one, for the overseer's own logic

The overseer cases need a gatekeeper that refuses an observer on command. Every shipping public
gatekeeper can do that only at a cost that would dominate the test:

- **OAuth gatekeepers** need a whole vendor auth surface mocked before an account exists at all.
- **The Context Library** only refuses once an observation has been *recorded*, which takes a gadget
  read session (so a Worker Loader), a slash-command invocation, or an AI-chat catalog snapshot. It is
  also a singleton, so it can never produce the two simultaneously-failing bindings one of these cases
  needs.

Adding a test hook to those workers was considered and rejected. A "mark observed" hook would stub the
very state the tracker maintains, making the test circular.

So `fixtures/gatekeeper-test/` is a real Worker speaking the real protocol, whose verification outcome
the tests set over an HTTP control route. **It is scoped to overseer logic, not a long-term substitute
for per-vendor coverage.** Testing actual gatekeepers is the expected trajectory, which is why the
harness takes a *list* of gatekeepers and the interceptor takes *pluggable* handler modules: a future
`gatekeeper-google` suite is "add `google-handlers.ts`, point the harness at the package" — the same
shape a consumer repo's per-vendor suite takes, with production code unmodified.

### Storage isolation is by convention, because the alternative is worse

`server.reset()` exists, and measuring it settles the question: **~3 s per call**, which is more than
an entire suite run. It also restarts the server — `server.url` becomes undefined and every open
WebSocket RPC session dies with "WebSocket connection failed". It is not a storage wipe you can use
between tests; it is a teardown.

So storage persists for the harness's lifetime and **no test may assume a clean slate**. Tests stay
independent by taking fresh identities: `nextUsernames()` from the toolkit, per-test resource URLs, and
account labels allocated by the connect/provision helper rather than chosen by the caller.

One corollary that is easy to get wrong: the "nothing escaped to the internet" assertion belongs in
`afterAll`, not `afterEach`. With `it.concurrent`, an `afterEach` fires while siblings are still
running, so it would inspect and clear state they are still using — and could discard an escape a
sibling was about to be blamed for.

### wrangler and workerd versions are coupled

The public repo pins `workerd` through a root `overrides` entry, which collapses every transitive
request to one version. A newer `wrangler` brings a newer `miniflare` that demands a newer `workerd`
than the override yields, and the harness then fails to boot:

```
The Workers runtime failed to start ... requires compatibility date "2026-07-08",
but the newest date supported by this server binary is "2026-06-30".
```

So the public package pins `wrangler` to `~4.104.0` — the release whose bundled `workerd` matches the
override. Bumping it means bumping the override in step.

### A consumer in another repo can end up with two copies of capnweb

A consumer repo installs its own workspace *and* the `public/` submodule's, as two separate pnpm
stores. So `capnweb` resolves to two different copies: the toolkit's `rpc-client` gets the
submodule's, while anything importing `capnweb` from one of the consumer's own packages gets the
other. A stub is only serialisable by the instance that owns the session, so mixing them fails:

```
TypeError: Cannot serialize value: [object RpcStub]
```

The trap is that a dev machine where a single `pnpm install` deduped both will not show this. It first
appeared in CI, which runs `pnpm install` and `pnpm --dir public install` separately. To reproduce
locally, do the same.

The toolkit therefore owns the capnweb boundary: mint callback stubs with `stubFor()` from
`rpc-client`, never with an imported `RpcStub`. Importing `RpcStub` as a *type* is fine. This is
enforced structurally in this repo — the lint rules in `vite.config.ts` restrict `capnweb` value
imports within this package to `rpc-client.ts` (`allowTypeImports` leaves type imports alone). A
consumer repo without a linter should treat the rule as a convention its test files follow via
`stubFor()`.

### Worker entry modules may export only classes and the default handler

workerd treats every named export of the entry module as an entrypoint. Exporting a plain string
constant from the fixture produced:

```
Incorrect type for map entry 'THING_URL_PATTERN': the provided value is not of
type 'function or ExportedHandler'.
```

Type-only exports are fine (they erase). Anything else has to stay module-private.

246:       if (started && !closed) {
247:         // this.ctx.abort() would be nicer here, but it is still marked experimental in the
248:         // workers runtime.
249:         this.abortSession(new Error(`lost connection to workspace DO (gadget ${id})`));
250:       }
251:     }
252: 
253:     let result;
254:     try {
255:       result = await overseer.open(userId, profileId, notifyClosed, shareKey, configureObservers);
256:     } catch (err) {
257:       // A denial proves this user's listing for the workspace is stale: revocation tries to drop it
258:       // (refreshAffectedCollaboratorListings), but that push is best-effort. Only catches entries
259:       // they click; others stay frozen at revocation, as a disconnected collaborator gets no pushes.
260:       if (getOpenGadgetErrorCode(err) === OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceAccessDenied) {
261:         await this.#user.forgetSharedGadget(id);
262:       }
263:       throw err;
264:     }
265:     started = true;
266:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
267:       event_name: "gadget_opened",
268:       user_id: userId,
269:       gadget_id: id,
270:       source: shareKey ? "share_key" : "direct",
271:     });
272:     return result;
273:   }

433:   async newGadgetFromBlueprint(
434:     blueprintId: string,
435:     bindings: Record<string, BlueprintBindingAssignment>
436:   ): Promise<RpcStub<Overseer>> {
437:     // 1. Read blueprint from KV.
438:     let kvRecord = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
439:     if (!kvRecord) throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
440: 
441:     // 2. Read gzip-compressed Yjs doc from R2 and decompress.
442:     let codeBytes = await readBlueprintContent(this.env, blueprintId, kvRecord.metadata.version);
443:     if (!codeBytes) throw new Error("Blueprint content not found in R2.");
444: 
445:     // 3. Create new Overseer DO (same as newGadget()).
446:     let id = this.overseers.newUniqueId().toString();
447:     await this.#user.newGadget(id, kvRecord.metadata.title);
448:     let overseerResult = await this.#openGadgetInternal(id);
449: 
450:     // 4. Initialize from blueprint code.
451:     let overseerDo = this.overseers.get(this.overseers.idFromString(id));
452:     await overseerDo.initializeFromBlueprint(codeBytes, kvRecord.metadata.title,
453:         deploymentOutputForBlueprint(await readAdminConfig(this.env), blueprintId,
454:             sanitizeBlueprintOutput(kvRecord.metadata.output)));
455: 
456:     // 5. Create gatekeepers from assignments and bind them into the workspace's (only) gadget.
457:     let metadata = await overseerResult.getMetadata();
458:     using gadget = await overseerResult.getGadget(metadata.defaultGadgetId!);
459: 
460:     // Defensively put blueprint bindings into a map (not a raw object) until we've had a chance to
461:     // validate the names.
462:     let blueprintBindings = new Map(Object.entries(kvRecord.metadata.bindings));
463:     let gadgetId = metadata.defaultGadgetId!;
464: 
465:     // Create gatekeepers in two phases: first every non-spawner binding (binding the
466:     // non-spawnerOnly ones into the gadget, and recording each created gatekeeper's id by
467:     // binding name), then the agent spawners, whose configs reference the phase-one results
468:     // symbolically (see SpawnerEnvTarget).
469:     let createdIds = new Map<string, WorkpieceId>();
470:     let gkPromises: Promise<void>[] = [];
471: 
472:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
473:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
474:       if (!blueprintBinding) {
475:         throw new Error(`Unknown binding name: ${bindingName}`);
476:       }
477: 
478:       gkPromises.push((async () => {
479:         let gk;
480:         if (assignment.type === "gatekeeper") {
481:           gk = await overseerResult.newGatekeeper(assignment.accountId, assignment.resourceUrl);
482:           if (!gk) {
483:             throw new Error(`Failed to create gatekeeper for binding "${bindingName}".`);
484:           }
485:         } else if (assignment.type === "aiModel") {
486:           gk = await overseerResult.newAiModelGatekeeper(assignment.modelId);
487:         } else {
488:           return;  // agent spawners are created in phase two
489:         }
490:         try {
491:           let id = await gk.getId();
492:           createdIds.set(bindingName, id);
493:           // A spawnerOnly binding exists purely to feed some spawner's env; it is not bound
494:           // into the gadget itself.
495:           if (!blueprintBinding.spawnerOnly) {
496:             await gadget.bind(bindingName, id);
497:           }
498:         } finally {
499:           gk[Symbol.dispose]();
500:         }
501:       })());
502:     }
503: 
504:     await Promise.all(gkPromises);
505: 
506:     // Phase two: agent spawners, with the full AgentSpawnerConfig reconstructed -- displayName
507:     // from the binding's title, modelId from the assignment, and env resolved against the
508:     // phase-one gatekeepers and the new gadget.
509:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
510:       if (assignment.type !== "agentSpawner") continue;
511:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
512:       if (blueprintBinding?.type !== "agentSpawner") {
513:         throw new Error(`Binding "${bindingName}" type mismatch.`);
514:       }
515: 
516:       let env: Record<string, WorkpieceId> = {};
517:       for (let [envName, target] of Object.entries(blueprintBinding.env)) {
518:         if (target.type === "gadget") {
519:           env[envName] = gadgetId;
520:         } else {
521:           let id = createdIds.get(target.name);
522:           if (id === undefined) {
523:             throw new Error(`Agent spawner binding "${bindingName}" references binding ` +
524:                 `"${target.name}", which was not assigned.`);
525:           }
526:           env[envName] = id;
527:         }
528:       }
529: 
530:       let config: AgentSpawnerConfig = {
531:         displayName: blueprintBinding.title,
532:         modelId: assignment.modelId,
533:         env,
534:       };
535:       using gk = await overseerResult.newAgentSpawnerGatekeeper(config);
536:       await gadget.bind(bindingName, await gk.getId());
537:     }
538: 
539:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
540:       event_name: "gadget_created",
541:       user_id: this.#userId.toString(),
542:       gadget_id: id,
543:       blueprint_id: blueprintId,
544:       source: "blueprint",
545:     });
546: 
547:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC stubs are compatible but the type
548:     //     system doesn't know this.
549:     return overseerResult;
550:   }

652:   async startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId: string): Promise<{ url: string; attempt: RpcStub<LoginAttempt> }> {
653:     if (!getAuthGatekeeperAllowlist(this.env).includes(vendorId)) {
654:       throw new Error(`Sign-in via "${vendorId}" is not enabled on this deployment.`);
655:     }
656:     const vendor = getAuthVendorBinding(this.env, vendorId);
657:     if (!vendor) throw new Error(`No such auth gatekeeper: ${vendorId}`);
658:     const desc = await vendor.describe();
659:     if (!desc.providesAuth) throw new Error(`"${vendorId}" does not provide authentication.`);
660: 
661:     // The PendingLogin DO is the rendezvous between this request and the (separate) OAuth-callback
662:     // invocation. The client never sees its id — we hand back an `attempt` stub instead.
663:     const pendingId = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.newUniqueId();
664:     const pending = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.get(pendingId);
665:     const callback = this.ctx.exports.LoginConnectCallbackImpl(
666:         { props: { pendingId: pendingId.toString(), vendorId } });
667:     // For most providers, sign-in needs only minimal scopes to verify the user's email (the grant is
668:     // transient); capability scopes are requested later via an explicit connectAccount. Cloudflare is
669:     // the exception: signing in with Cloudflare also links AI Gateway billing, so it requests and
670:     // persists the billing-only scope set up front.
671:     const options = vendorId === CLOUDFLARE_VENDOR_ID
672:       ? { scopes: "full" as const, resourceUrlPatterns: [] }
673:       : { scopes: "auth" as const };
674:     const { url } = await vendor.connectAccount(callback, options);
675:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC targets are compatible but the type
676:     //     system doesn't know this.
677:     return { url, attempt: new LoginAttemptImpl(pending) };
678:   }

658:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
659:   // Free-tier daily LLM-call counter (folded in from the former standalone RateLimitDO). Only used
660:   // when ENABLE_CLOUDFLARE_LIMITS is on. Single-threaded DO execution makes the read-modify-write
661:   // race-free; the window resets at UTC midnight when the stored day no longer matches.
662:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
663: 
664:   #dailyUsed(day: string): number {
665:     let record = this.storage.dailyLlmCount.get();
666:     return record && record.day === day ? record.count : 0;
667:   }
668: 
669:   /** Read the current daily quota state without counting a call. */
670:   async checkDailyLlmCount(limit: number): Promise<DailyQuotaResult> {
671:     let day = utcDayKey();
672:     let used = this.#dailyUsed(day);
673:     return { withinLimits: used < limit, remaining: Math.max(0, limit - used), limit, used,
674:              resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
675:   }
676: 
677:   /**
678:    * Atomically check the daily limit and, if within it, count one call. `withinLimits` is the
679:    * pre-count decision; `used`/`remaining` reflect the state AFTER counting. No-ops once exhausted,
680:    * so a blocked request never counts.
681:    */
682:   async consumeDailyLlmCall(limit: number): Promise<DailyQuotaResult> {
683:     let day = utcDayKey();
684:     let used = this.#dailyUsed(day);
685:     if (used >= limit) {
686:       return { withinLimits: false, remaining: 0, limit, used, resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
687:     }
688:     let newUsed = used + 1;
689:     this.storage.dailyLlmCount.put({ day, count: newUsed });
690:     return { withinLimits: true, remaining: Math.max(0, limit - newUsed), limit, used: newUsed,
691:              resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
692:   }

797:   /**
798:    * Replace the set of outputs recorded for one workspace. Called by that workspace's Overseer
799:    * whenever its gadget registry changes and whenever it is opened.
800:    *
801:    * A workspace the user no longer tracks (deleted, or a shared one they dismissed) has its
802:    * entries dropped.
803:    */
804:   syncWorkspaceOutputs(workspaceId: string, entries: WorkspaceOutputEntry[]): void {
805:     this.storage.outputs.byWorkspace.delete(workspaceId);
806:     if (!this.storage.gadgets.get(workspaceId)) return;
807:     for (let entry of entries) {

810:   }

812:   async listOutputs(): Promise<ListOutputsResult> {
813:     let catchingUp = await this.#backfillOutputs();
814:     return {outputs: this.#readOutputs(), catchingUp};
815:   }
816: 
817:   // Ask the user's pre-existing workspaces to populate the outputs index, once. Workspaces push as
818:   // they change and when opened, so only those predating the index need this.
819:   //
820:   // Sweeps one bounded page and reports whether more remains, rather than sweeping everything: a
821:   // first Outputs load must not wait on every workspace the user has ever created. The caller
822:   // drains the rest, so the list fills in while the page is open.
823:   async #backfillOutputs(): Promise<boolean> {
824:     if (this.storage.outputsBackfilled.get()) return false;
825: 
826:     let startAfter = this.storage.outputsBackfillCursor.get() || undefined;
827:     let cursor = startAfter ?? "";
828:     let targets: string[] = [];
829:     let examined = 0;
830:     for (let gadget of this.storage.gadgets.list({startAfter, limit: OUTPUTS_BACKFILL_PAGE})) {
831:       ++examined;
832:       cursor = gadget.id;
833:       // A shared workspace is mirrored on open, not swept; a half-created one has nothing yet.
834:       if (!gadget.owner && isFullyCreated(gadget)) targets.push(gadget.id);
835:     }
836:     let done = examined < OUTPUTS_BACKFILL_PAGE;
837: 
838:     let ownerId = this.ctx.id.toString();
839:     let overseers = this.ctx.exports.OverseerDurableObject;
840:     let results = await Promise.allSettled(targets.map(id =>
841:         overseers.get(overseers.idFromString(id)).getOutputsForOwnerBackfill(ownerId)));
842: 
843:     let failureCount = 0;
844:     let firstError: unknown;
845:     for (let [index, result] of results.entries()) {
846:       if (result.status === "fulfilled") {
847:         if (result.value) this.syncWorkspaceOutputs(targets[index], result.value);
848:       } else {
849:         if (failureCount === 0) firstError = result.reason;
850:         ++failureCount;
851:       }
852:     }
853: 
854:     if (failureCount > 0) {
855:       logger.warn("failed to backfill outputs for some workspaces", {
856:         event: "outputs.backfill.partial",
857:         failureCount,
858:         error: firstError,
859:       });
860:     }
861: 
862:     // Advance past workspaces that failed, rather than retrying them. The index is self-healing,
863:     // so one missed here reappears the moment it is touched, whereas holding the cursor lets a
864:     // single unwakeable workspace stall the sweep forever.
865:     if (done) {
866:       this.storage.outputsBackfilled.put(true);
867:     } else {
868:       this.storage.outputsBackfillCursor.put(cursor);
869:     }
870: 
871:     // A page where everything failed looks systemic, so stop draining and let the next visit pick
872:     // up from the next page: draining on would be a burst of doomed calls during an outage.
873:     if (failureCount > 0 && failureCount === targets.length) return false;
874:     return !done;
875:   }
876: 
877:   #readOutputs(): OutputSummary[] {
878:     let result: OutputSummary[] = [];
879:     for (let output of this.storage.outputs.list()) {
880:       let workspace = this.storage.gadgets.get(output.workspaceId);
881:       if (!workspace || !isFullyCreated(workspace)) continue;
882:       result.push({
883:         workspaceId: output.workspaceId,
884:         workpieceId: output.workpieceId,
885:         ...(output.output ? {output: output.output} : {}),
886:         title: output.title,
887:         workspaceTitle: workspace.title,
888:         created: output.created,
889:         lastActive: workspace.lastActive,
890:         ...(workspace.owner ? {owner: workspace.owner} : {}),
891:         ...(workspace.role ? {role: workspace.role} : {}),
892:       });
893:     }
894:     result.sort((a, b) => b.lastActive.getTime() - a.lastActive.getTime());
895:     return result;
896:   }

1000:       // Delete all R2 objects with the blueprint ID prefix.
1001:       for (let v = 1; v <= kvRecord.metadata.version; v++) {
1002:         await this.env.BLUEPRINT_CONTENT.delete(`${id}/${v}`);
1003:       }

1009:

192:     config: AdminConfig, blueprintId: string, declared: BlueprintOutput | undefined)
193:     : BlueprintOutput | undefined {
194:   return resolveFormatOutput(declared, config.formats.find(f => f.blueprintId === blueprintId)?.overrides);
195: }
196: 
197: /**
198:  * Resolve what a promoted blueprint should be shown as: the blueprint's own declaration with the
199:  * deployment's overrides applied. Returns undefined when the blueprint declares nothing and the
200:  * admin overrode nothing meaningful.
201:  */
202: export function resolveFormatOutput(
203:     declared: BlueprintOutput | undefined, overrides?: Partial<BlueprintOutput>)
204:     : BlueprintOutput | undefined {
205:   let merged = {...declared, ...overrides};
206:   if (!merged.id || !merged.noun || !merged.plural || !merged.icon) return undefined;
207:   return merged as BlueprintOutput;
208: }
209: 
210: // --- Reading the promoted set ---
211: //
212: // Three surfaces offer the deployment's formats -- the user's New menu, the agent's catalog, and
213: // the admin panel that curates them.
214: 
215: /** One promoted blueprint joined with the blueprint it points at. */
216: export type PromotedFormat = {
217:   entry: FormatCuration;
218: 
219:   /**
220:    * The blueprint's own metadata. Absent when it has been deleted since being promoted; such an
221:    * entry is skipped everywhere except the admin panel, which offers to remove it.
222:    */
223:   metadata?: BlueprintMetadata;
224: 
225:   /** What the blueprint declares it produces, after validation. Absent if it declares nothing usable. */
226:   declared?: BlueprintOutput;
227: 
228:   /** `declared` with the deployment's overrides applied. */
229:   output?: BlueprintOutput;
230: };
231: 
232: /** Join promoted entries with the blueprints they point at, preserving order. */
233: export async function listPromotedFormats(env: BlueprintKvEnv, formats: FormatCuration[])
234:     : Promise<PromotedFormat[]> {
235:   let records = await Promise.all(
236:       formats.map(entry => readBlueprintKvRecord(env, entry.blueprintId)));
237: 
238:   return formats.map((entry, i) => {
239:     let metadata = records[i]?.metadata;
240:     let declared = sanitizeBlueprintOutput(metadata?.output);
241:     return {entry, metadata, declared, output: resolveFormatOutput(declared, entry.overrides)};
242:   });
243: }
244: 
245: /**
246:  * A format the deployment is offering, plus the two things only the agent's catalog wants: the
247:  * admin's note about when to prefer it, and the bindings its blueprint expects to be wired up.
248:  * listOutputFormats() drops both.
249:  */
250: export type FormatOffer = OutputFormatOffer & {
251:   agentHint?: string;
252:   bindings: Record<string, BlueprintBinding>;
253: };
254: 
255: /**
256:  * The formats this deployment offers, in menu order: promoted, enabled, and resolvable to a
257:  * complete presentation. A promoted blueprint that has since been deleted, or that names nothing
258:  * to call itself, is silently skipped.
259:  */
260: export async function listFormatOffers(env: BlueprintKvEnv, config: AdminConfig)
261:     : Promise<FormatOffer[]> {
262:   let enabled = config.formats.filter(entry => entry.enabled);
263:   if (enabled.length === 0) return [];
264: 
265:   let offers: FormatOffer[] = [];
266:   for (let {entry, metadata, output} of await listPromotedFormats(env, enabled)) {
267:     if (!metadata || !output) continue;
268:     offers.push({
269:       blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
270:       output,
271:       description: metadata.description,
272:       requiresSetup: Object.keys(metadata.bindings).length > 0,
273:       bindings: metadata.bindings,
274:       ...(entry.agentHint ? {agentHint: entry.agentHint} : {}),
275:     });
276:   }
277:   return offers;
278: }
279: 
280: function strings(value: unknown): string[] {
281:   return Array.isArray(value) ? value.filter((v): v is string => typeof v === "string") : [];
282: }
283: 
284: export function parseAdminConfig(raw: string | null): AdminConfig {
285:   if (!raw) return { ...DEFAULT_ADMIN_CONFIG };
286:   try {
287:     let p = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<AdminConfig>;
288:     let disabledResources: Record<string, string[]> = {};
289:     if (p.disabledResources && typeof p.disabledResources === "object") {
290:       for (let [vendorId, patterns] of Object.entries(p.disabledResources)) {
291:         let list = strings(patterns);
292:         if (list.length > 0) disabledResources[vendorId] = list;
293:       }
294:     }
295:     let ambientGatekeeperModes: Record<string, AmbientGatekeeperMode> = {};
296:     if (p.ambientGatekeeperModes && typeof p.ambientGatekeeperModes === "object") {
297:       for (let [vendorId, mode] of Object.entries(p.ambientGatekeeperModes)) {
298:         if (isAmbientGatekeeperMode(mode)) ambientGatekeeperModes[vendorId.toLowerCase()] = mode;
299:       }
300:     }
301:     return {
302:       signupsEnabled: typeof p.signupsEnabled === "boolean" ? p.signupsEnabled : true,
303:       siteName: typeof p.siteName === "string" ? p.siteName : "",
304:       siteLogoConfigured: typeof p.siteLogoConfigured === "boolean" ? p.siteLogoConfigured : false,
305:       instanceInstructions: typeof p.instanceInstructions === "string" ? p.instanceInstructions : "",
306:       announcement: typeof p.announcement === "string" ? p.announcement : "",
307:       banner: {
308:         text: typeof p.banner?.text === "string" ? p.banner.text : "",
309:         color: isBannerColor(p.banner?.color) ? p.banner!.color : DEFAULT_BANNER_COLOR,
310:       },
311:       accentColor: typeof p.accentColor === "string" ? p.accentColor : "",
312:       disabledResources,
313:       disabledGatekeepers: strings(p.disabledGatekeepers).map(v => v.toLowerCase()),
314:       ambientGatekeeperModes,
315:       formats: parseFormats(p.formats),
316:     };
317:   } catch {
318:     return { ...DEFAULT_ADMIN_CONFIG };
319:   }
320: }
321: 
322: export function serializeAdminConfig(config: AdminConfig): string {
323:   return JSON.stringify(config);
324: }
325: 
326: /** Read the admin config from the KV mirror. Cheap enough for the hot path (a single KV get). */
327: export async function readAdminConfig(env: Cloudflare.Env): Promise<AdminConfig> {
328:   return parseAdminConfig(await env.BLUEPRINTS.get(ADMIN_CONFIG_KEY));
329: }
330: 
331: // --- Resource-disable helpers ---
332: 
333: export function isResourceDisabled(
334:     config: AdminConfig, vendorId: string, urlPattern: string): boolean {
335:   return config.disabledResources[vendorId]?.includes(urlPattern) ?? false;
336: }
337: 
338: export function filterEnabledResources(
339:     config: AdminConfig, vendorId: string, resources: SupportedResource[]): SupportedResource[] {
340:   let disabled = config.disabledResources[vendorId];
341:   if (!disabled || disabled.length === 0) return resources;
342:   return resources.filter(r => !disabled.includes(r.urlPattern));
343: }
344: 
345: // --- Agent system-prompt instructions ---
346: 
347: /**
348:  * Wrap the admin instructions in a clearly-delimited block for the system prompt, or "" when unset.
349:  * Callers are responsible for separating this from the preceding prompt with a blank line.
350:  */
351: export function formatInstanceInstructions(instructions: string): string {
352:   let trimmed = instructions.trim();
353:   if (!trimmed) return "";
354:   return `# Deployment-specific instructions\n\n` +
355:       `The administrator of this deployment has provided the following additional instructions. ` +
356:       `Follow them unless they conflict with the user's safety or the instructions above.\n\n` +
357:       `<deployment_instructions>\n${trimmed}\n</deployment_instructions>`;
358: }

gatekeepers. Not a Worker: a library both of them import.

| Package | Endpoint comes from | Grant is scoped to |

wiring. A Worker's own vendor entrypoint, Durable Object classes and migrations, `Env`, connect
form, and configurator UI stay in the connector. Where a connector must vary shared behaviour it
does so through a named hook (`staticToken`, `mintAccount`), not a private copy.

## Modules

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `client` | Bounded Streamable HTTP transport (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`) using official MCP wire types |
| `oauth` | Small adapter around the official MCP client's OAuth errors and token revocation gap |
| `tools` | The trust boundary: read/action classification, auto-approval eligibility, approval prompts, catalog fingerprinting |
| `schema-to-ts` | JSON Schema to TypeScript, strict `callTool` overloads plus progressive discovery |
| `session-methods` | Installs those methods at runtime, so the generated types are not a fiction |
| `tool-search` | The one query matcher every catalog search uses, so a query cannot mean two things |
| `portal` | Gateway detection, tool-name to upstream-server mapping, server listing |
| `scope` | The resource-URL scope grammar, and the check every call passes through |
| `endpoint` | Validation and host blocklist for a user-supplied endpoint |
| `fetch` | Every outbound request; redirects are followed by hand and each hop re-checked, including SDK OAuth fetches |
| `account` | Durable Object base and persisted SDK OAuth state: connect, refresh, revocation |
| `facet` | Common session, catalog, action, and sharing behavior for connector-owned Durable Object facets |
| `catalog` | One binding's tool list: fetched, cached, scoped to the grant, classified; plus the cache for tools hydrated past that list |
| `connection` | `withClient` — transport sessions, retries, credential-expiry reporting |
| `action-store` | Staged to applied/rejected/failed, with a bound on what is retained and a claim so one approval is never sent twice |
| `session` | The Gadget-facing capability, and the one path every tool call takes |
| `sharing-policy` | The owner-only sharing rule |
| `html` | The connect-flow pages, so both connectors look like one product |
| `http` | Base-path, OAuth callback, and connect-link routing shared by both Workers |
| `log` | The field vocabulary both connectors log against |
| `user` | The common account description, revocation, and reconnect lifecycle |
| `util` | Hex encoding, host extraction, binding-name slugs; no policy |
| `types.d.ts` | Base types prepended to every generated per-server `.d.ts` |

Nothing outside `tools.ts` reads a tool's `annotations`.

## Trust tiers

A tier governs how far a server's own claims about its tools are believed. MCP's own guidance is
that a client must treat tool annotations as untrusted unless they come from a trusted server, and
the tier is where this deployment records which servers those are. It is named by provenance, is
deployment configuration rather than account state, and is read at each point of use so withdrawing
it takes effect at once.

- **`byo`** — a user typed the URL in. `readOnlyHint` classifies reads; nothing the server says can
  auto-apply a write.
- **`vetted`** — a deployment has asserted this endpoint's annotations can be relied on, so
  `destructiveHint: false` plus `idempotentHint: true` may drive auto-approval. Configuring an
  endpoint is not by itself enough to earn this: a portal aggregates upstream servers whose
  annotations the administrator never saw, which is why `gatekeeper-mcp-portal` defaults to `byo`
  and requires `MCP_PORTAL_TRUST_ANNOTATIONS=true`.

Honouring `readOnlyHint` on `byo` is a tradeoff, not a free win: a tool the server mislabels runs
with no approval, where an unlabelled one would have been queued. It is accepted because prompting
on every read makes the connector unusable for its main purpose, and because the owner chose to
connect the server. Auto-applying a write is not accepted on those terms.

Annotations are optional in MCP and most servers publish none. Every hint is compared with
`=== true` or `=== false`, so an unannotated tool is an action, needs approval, and can never
auto-apply, on either tier. That matches the spec's own defaults (`readOnlyHint: false`,
`destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: false`).

Neither tier can be shared. A Gadget bound to any MCP endpoint is owner-only, for reasons unrelated
to provenance — see [`sharing-policy.ts`](src/sharing-policy.ts).

What an account records instead of a tier is `provenance`, `"user"` or `"deployment"`, settled when
it connects. Provenance decides whether a server may rename itself over an administrator's chosen
label in an approval prompt, which is a question that should not move when an annotation setting
does.

## Applying an approved call

The guarantee is *at most once*, not exactly once. MCP has no idempotency key that would make a
repeated call harmless and no inverse operation that would undo one, so where the two conflict the
store prefers losing a result over repeating a write.

An approval is claimed in storage before the call is sent, which is what stops two concurrent
`applyAction` calls from both reaching the server. Once the call returns, the record is settled in
its own small write *before* the result is attached, so nothing about handling a server-controlled

lose the fact that the write already happened.

Failures are split by what the server is known to have done, because that is not something the
caller can work out afterwards. Only a `401` or `403` proves the tool was refused before dispatch.

leave the outcome unknown; those are closed as failed and **not** retryable, since the request may
already have been carried out. The classification (`callMayHaveTakenEffect`) fails safe: anything it
cannot positively identify as declined counts as possibly performed.

The same rule covers an activation dying between sending the call and recording the reply. The claim
is not released for another attempt: after `APPLY_CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS` the action is closed the same

So the cost of a network blip is a call someone has to stage again, deliberately. That is the trade
this module makes everywhere: an approval is never spent twice without a person saying so.

| Search query / results | 200 chars / 20 tools | `tool-search.ts` | Bounds agent-supplied matching work and the summaries returned to it |
| Hydrated definitions per facet | 200 tools / 1 MiB | `catalog.ts` | Bounds definitions fetched individually beyond the described catalog |
| Tool description | 4 KB | `client.ts` | As above, per tool, before it reaches storage |
| Tool input schema | 20 KB | `client.ts` | Dropped rather than clipped; half a schema is not a schema |
| `tools/list` pages | 50 | `client.ts` | Stops a cursor that never ends; exhaustion truncates catalogs and fails exact/search discovery as a scan limit |
| Response body | 1 MiB | `fetch.ts` | Every response is buffered whole before it can be parsed, and a `tools/call` result is otherwise unbounded |
| Bounded outbound operation | 30 seconds | `fetch.ts` | OAuth and discovery callers opt into one deadline covering redirects, pagination, body streaming, and session retry |
| Retained result | 128 KB | `action-store.ts` | Held until the Gadget collects it; oversized ones are replaced by a note |
| Retained actions | 100 | `action-store.ts` | Records are for collecting a result, not an audit log |
| Actions awaiting a decision | 50 | `action-store.ts` | These cannot be pruned, so uncapped they are an unbounded write |

| Tool arguments in a prompt | 4000 chars | `tools.ts` | Agent-controlled text in the same decision |
| Server name | 60 chars | `account.ts` | As above; also stripped of Markdown |
| Redirect hops | 3 | `fetch.ts` | Each one re-checked; more is a loop, not a deployment |
| Connect link | 10 min | `connect-nonce.ts` | Single-use, and consumed on success |
| Unfinished connect | 1 hour | `connect-nonce.ts` | After which a half-built account deletes itself |

1: // The public origin of a gadgets instance. Routes by path prefix to the workshop backend and
2: // whichever gatekeepers are bound, and serves the workshop frontend for everything else.
3: //
4: // Routing config IS the binding set: gatekeepers are discovered by scanning `GATEKEEPER_*` env
5: // keys, so installing a gatekeeper only requires re-deploying this worker with one more service
6: // binding — no code or config changes here.
7: //
8: // The same worker doubles as the dev router (`pnpm dev-server` at the repo root): dev has no
9: // `ASSETS` binding, so frontend requests fall through to the backend instead.
10: 
11: // gatekeeper-email's entrypoint: a WorkerEntrypoint whose optional email() handler is present.
12: type EmailEntrypoint = CloudflareWorkersModule.WorkerEntrypoint &
13:     Required<Pick<CloudflareWorkersModule.WorkerEntrypoint, "email">>;
14: 
15: export interface Env {
16:   WORKSHOP_BACKEND: Fetcher;
17:   /** Present in production (wrangler.jsonc assets stanza); absent in dev. */
18:   ASSETS?: Fetcher;
19:   /** Dormant until custom domains + Email Routing exist; the handler ships anyway. */
20:   GATEKEEPER_EMAIL?: Service<EmailEntrypoint>;
21:   [key: string]: unknown;
22: }
23: 
24: export default {
25:   async fetch(req, env) {
26:     const url = new URL(req.url);
27: 
28:     for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {
29:       if (!key.startsWith("GATEKEEPER_")) continue;
30:       const suffix = key.slice("GATEKEEPER_".length).toLowerCase().replaceAll("_", "-");
31:       const prefix = `/gatekeeper/${suffix}`;
32:       if (url.pathname === prefix || url.pathname.startsWith(prefix + "/")) {
33:         return (env[key] as Fetcher).fetch(req);
34:       }
35:     }
36: 
37:     if (url.pathname === "/api" || url.pathname.startsWith("/api/") ||
38:         url.pathname === "/blueprint-screenshot" ||
39:         url.pathname.startsWith("/blueprint-screenshot/")) {
40:       return env.WORKSHOP_BACKEND.fetch(req);
41:     }
42: 
43:     // Note: gatekeeper OAuth redirects land on the gatekeeper Workers themselves, at
44:     // `/gatekeeper/<name>/oauth` (handled by the loop above) — there are no backend /auth
45:     // callbacks.
46: 
47:     if (env.ASSETS) {
48:       return env.ASSETS.fetch(req);
49:     }
50: 
51:     // Dev only: with no assets binding here, everything else goes to the backend.
52:     //
53:     // In `run-local` mode the backend has a static `assets` binding configured (with
54:     // `run_worker_first` for the API routes), so it serves the pre-built single-page app for these
55:     // frontend requests. In normal dev mode the backend has no assets and frontend requests aren't
56:     // expected here -- run the Vite dev server with `pnpm dev-client` and open localhost:3000
57:     // directly instead. (We don't try to forward to localhost:3000 becaues it doesn't work well:
58:     // Vite's HMR socket gets disconnected every time wrangler restarts workerd.)
59:     return env.WORKSHOP_BACKEND.fetch(req);
60:   },
61: 
62:   async email(message, env) {
63:     if (!env.GATEKEEPER_EMAIL) {
64:       message.setReject("No email gatekeeper is installed on this instance.");
65:       return;
66:     }
67:     await env.GATEKEEPER_EMAIL.email(message);
68:   },
69: } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

69: const CONTEXT_LIBRARY_TYPES = `

71:  * Shared context documents and skills. Catalog entries provide document IDs accepted by read().
72:  * Each call records an observation.
73:  */
74: interface ContextLibrary {
75:   /** Full-text search across the collections available to you. Returns documents (with docIds). */
76:   search(query: string, opts?: { collectionId?: string; limit?: number }): Promise<ContextSearchResult[]>;
77:   /** Browse the tree: no args lists collections (by collectionId); pass a collectionId (and optional
78:    *  path) to drill in and get the documents (with docIds) inside it. */
79:   list(opts?: { collectionId?: string; path?: string }): Promise<ContextListing>;
80:   /** Read a document by an ID from the catalog, search(), or list(). */
81:   read(docId: string): Promise<ContextDocument | null>;
82: }
83: 
84: interface ContextSearchResult {
85:   docId: string;          // opaque id to pass to read()
86:   collectionId?: string;
87:   title: string;
88:   path?: string;          // e.g. "billing/revenue.md"
89:   description?: string;
90:   snippet?: string;       // matched excerpt
91:   score?: number;         // higher is more relevant
92: }

94: type ContextListingEntry =
95:   // A collection: its id is a collectionId — pass it to list()/search() to see inside, not read().
96:   | { type: "collection"; id: string; title: string; description?: string; documentCount: number }
97:   | { type: "directory"; path: string; name: string }
98:   // A document: its docId is what read() takes.
99:   | { type: "document"; docId: string; path: string; name: string; description?: string; contentType?: string };

101: interface ContextListing {
102:   collectionId?: string;
103:   path?: string;
104:   entries: ContextListingEntry[];
105: }

108:   docId: string;
109:   title: string;
110:   path?: string;
111:   description?: string;
112:   content: string;        // text (markdown/etc.) or a data: URI for binary content

202:     extends WorkerEntrypoint<Cloudflare.Env, ContextAccountProps>
203:     implements ContextVerifierApi {
204:   async hasCollectionAccess(sharingDomain: string, collectionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
205:     if (sharingDomain !== this.ctx.props.sharingDomain) return false;
206:     let userLibraries = this.ctx.exports.UserLibraryDurableObject;
207:     let registries = this.ctx.exports.LibraryRegistryDurableObject;
208:     let [owns, isPublic] = await Promise.all([
209:       userLibraries.get(userLibraries.idFromName(
210:         domainName(sharingDomain, this.ctx.props.accountId))).hasOwned(collectionId),

219: export class ContextGatekeeper
220:     extends DurableObject<Cloudflare.Env, ContextAccountProps>
221:     implements Gatekeeper<LibraryReadSession> {
222:   #collections() { return this.ctx.exports.ContextCollectionDurableObject; }
223:   #userLibraries() { return this.ctx.exports.UserLibraryDurableObject; }
224:   #observers() {
225:     return new ContextObserverTracker(this.ctx.storage.kv, this.ctx.props.sharingDomain);
226:   }
227: 
228:   async #loadSkills(
229:       collections: EnabledCollectionInfo[]):
230:       Promise<CollectionSkills[]> {
231:     let result: CollectionSkills[] = [];
232:     for (let offset = 0; offset < collections.length; offset += COLLECTION_SKILL_FANOUT) {
233:       let batch = await Promise.all(
234:         collections.slice(offset, offset + COLLECTION_SKILL_FANOUT).map(async collection => {
235:           try {
236:             let id = this.#collections().idFromName(
237:                 domainName(this.ctx.props.sharingDomain, collection.id));
238:             let skills = await this.#collections().get(id).listAgentSkills();
239:             return {collection, skills};
240:           } catch (error) {
241:             console.error("Failed to load skills from Context collection:", {
242:               collectionId: collection.id,
243:               error,
244:             });
245:             return null;
246:           }
247:         }));
248:       for (let entry of batch) {
249:         if (entry) result.push(entry);
250:       }
251:     }
252:     return result;
253:   }
254: 
255:   async describe(): Promise<ResourceDescription> {
256:     return {
257:       url: "context://library",
258:       title: "Context",
259:       snippet: "Search and read your team's shared context collections.",
260:       suggestedBindingName: "CONTEXT",
261:       tsType: "ContextLibrary",
262:       hasSlashCommands: true,
263:     };
264:   }
265: 
266:   async getTypeScriptTypes(): Promise<string> {
267:     return CONTEXT_LIBRARY_TYPES;
268:   }

270:   #newReadSession(authorizer: NativeRpcStub<ObservationAuthorizer>): LibraryReadSession {
271:     // The read session uses this authorizer after startSession() returns, so it owns a duplicate.
272:     let ownedAuthorizer = authorizer.dup();
273:     try {
274:       return new LibraryReadSession(
275:         this.#collections(), this.#userLibraries(),
276:         this.ctx.props.sharingDomain, this.ctx.props.accountId, ownedAuthorizer,
277:         collectionIds => this.#observers().prepareObservation(collectionIds));
278:     } catch (err) {
279:       ownedAuthorizer[Symbol.dispose]?.();
280:       throw err;
281:     }
282:   }
283: 
284:   async startSession(approvalQueue: NativeRpcStub<ApprovalQueue>): Promise<LibraryReadSession> {
285:     return this.#newReadSession(approvalQueue);
286:   }
287: 
288:   async getSlashCommandProvider():
289:       Promise<ContextSlashCommandProvider> {
290:     return new ContextSlashCommandProvider(
291:         () => this.#listSlashCommands(),
292:         (id, args, authorizer) => this.#invokeAgentSkillCommand(id, args, authorizer));
293:   }
294: 
295:   async #listSlashCommands(): Promise<SlashCommandDescriptor[]> {
296:     let domain = this.ctx.props.sharingDomain;
297:     let userLibrary = this.#userLibraries().get(
298:         this.#userLibraries().idFromName(domainName(domain, this.ctx.props.accountId)));
299:     let collections = (await loadEnabledContextCollections(this.env, domain, userLibrary))
300:         .toSorted((left, right) =>
301:           left.title.localeCompare(right.title) || left.id.localeCompare(right.id));
302:     return buildAgentSkillCommands(await this.#loadSkills(collections));
303:   }
304: 
305:   async #invokeAgentSkillCommand(
306:       id: string, args: string, authorizer: NativeRpcStub<ObservationAuthorizer>):
307:       Promise<SlashCommandResult> {
308:     using session = this.#newReadSession(authorizer);
309:     let document = await session.read(id);
310:     if (!document?.path) throw new Error("The selected Agent Skill is no longer available.");
311:     let manifest = parseSkillManifest(document.path, document.content);
312:     return {
313:       skillName: manifest.name,
314:       message: buildAgentSkillMessage(id, document.content, args),
315:     };
316:   }
317: 
318:   async getAgentCatalog(
319:       authorizer: NativeRpcStub<ObservationAuthorizer>): Promise<AgentCatalog> {
320:     let domain = this.ctx.props.sharingDomain;
321:     let userLibrary = this.#userLibraries().get(
322:       this.#userLibraries().idFromName(domainName(domain, this.ctx.props.accountId)));
323:     let collections = await loadEnabledContextCollections(this.env, domain, userLibrary);
324:     let catalog = buildContextCatalog(collections, await this.#loadSkills(collections));
325:     if (catalog.entries.length > 0) {
326:       let collectionIds = [...new Set(catalog.entries.map(entry => {
327:         let slash = entry.id.indexOf("/");
328:         return slash < 0 ? entry.id : entry.id.slice(0, slash);
329:       }))];
330:       let check = await this.#observers().prepareObservation(collectionIds);
331:       await authorizer.authorizeObservation({
332:         title: "Context catalog",
333:         description: `Listed ${catalog.entries.length} available Context item(s).`,
334:         excludeObservers: check.excludeObservers,
335:       });
336:       check.commit();
337:     }
338:     return catalog;
339:   }

344:   }

135:         if (!isTerminal(state)) {

137:             capabilitiesKey(activation.workspaceId, activation.scheduleId),
138:             { initiator },
139:           );
140:         }
141:       });
142:     } finally {
143:       disposeCapabilities(replaced);
144:     }
145:     await this.#planAlarmAfterMutation();

266:   async #runAlarm(): Promise<{
267:     dueCount: number;
268:     batchSize: number;
269:     backlogCount: number;
270:     startHookRejectedCount: number;
271:   }> {
272:     const now = Date.now();
273:     await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(checkedAdd(now, RECOVERY_DELAY_MS));
274:     if (this.#requireMetadata().revoked) {
275:       await this.#cleanupRevokedAccount();
276:       return { dueCount: 0, batchSize: 0, backlogCount: 0, startHookRejectedCount: 0 };
277:     }
278: 
279:     const due = this.#listSchedules()
280:       .filter(([, schedule]) => isDue(schedule, now))
281:       .toSorted(compareDueSchedules);
282:     const batch = due.slice(0, ALARM_BATCH_SIZE);
283: 
284:     // An alarm cannot overlap its own live handler, so an immediate write would not bypass a hung
285:     // callback. Rev1 relies on the recovery watchdog and replans after a successful batch.
286:     let startHookRejectedCount = 0;
287:     // A hung callback stalls this entire per-account batch. Stronger isolation is deferred beyond
288:     // rev1; ordinary work remains bounded to four concurrent deliveries.
289:     await runBounded(batch, DELIVERY_CONCURRENCY, async ([key, schedule]) => {
290:       if (await this.#deliverSafely(key, schedule)) startHookRejectedCount++;
291:     });
292:     await this.#planAlarm();
293:     return {
294:       dueCount: due.length,
295:       batchSize: batch.length,
296:       backlogCount: due.length - batch.length,
297:       startHookRejectedCount,
298:     };
299:   }

345:   /**
346:    * Applies a transition to the fenced pending run, then persists it. Releases the delivery
347:    * capability once the schedule reaches a state it can never fire from, after the commit.
348:    */
349:   #settle(
350:     prepared: PreparedRun,
351:     stage: PendingStage | undefined,
352:     transition: (state: PendingState) => EnabledSchedule,
353:   ): void {
354:     let orphaned: StoredCapabilities | undefined;
355:     this.ctx.storage.transactionSync(() => {
356:       if (this.#requireMetadata().revoked) return;
357:       const key = scheduleKey(prepared.workspaceId, prepared.scheduleId);
358:       const stored = this.#readSchedule(key);
359:       if (!matchesPending(stored, prepared)) return;
360:       if (stage !== undefined && stored.state.stage !== stage) return;
361:       const state = transition(stored.state);
362:       this.ctx.storage.kv.put<StoredSchedule>(key, { ...stored, state });
363:       if (isTerminal(state)) orphaned = this.#takeCapabilities(state);
364:     });
365:     disposeCapabilities(orphaned);
366:   }

368:   /** Removes a schedule's stored capability row, handing the stub back to the caller to dispose. */
369:   #takeCapabilities(state: EnabledSchedule): StoredCapabilities | undefined {
370:     const key = capabilitiesKey(state.workspaceId, state.scheduleId);
371:     const stored = this.ctx.storage.kv.get<StoredCapabilities>(key);
372:     if (stored) this.ctx.storage.kv.delete(key);
373:     return stored;
374:   }

376:   async #deliver(key: string): Promise<boolean> {
377:     const prepared = this.#prepareRun(key, Date.now());
378:     if (!prepared) return false;
379:     return obsContext.with({ runId: prepared.runId }, async () => {
380:       try {
381:         return await this.#deliverPrepared(prepared);
382:       } catch (error) {
383:         this.#reportDeliveryFailure(error);
384:         return false;
385:       }
386:     });
387:   }

389:   async #deliverPrepared(prepared: PreparedRun): Promise<boolean> {
390:     const capabilities = this.ctx.storage.kv.get<StoredCapabilities>(
391:       capabilitiesKey(prepared.workspaceId, prepared.scheduleId),
392:     );
393:     if (!capabilities) {
394:       const error = new Error("Scheduler capability record is missing.");
395:       logger.error("scheduler capability record is missing", {
396:         event: "scheduler.capabilities.missing",
397:         error,
398:       });
399:       reportIssue("scheduler.capabilities.missing", error, {
400:         handled: true,
401:         attributes: obsContext.get(),
402:       });
403:       this.#rejectPending(prepared, Date.now());
404:       return false;
405:     }
406: 
407:     let hookResult: HookResult | undefined;
408:     try {
409:       // @ts-expect-error Worker RPC promises are disposable even though the mapped type omits it.
410:       using hookCall = capabilities.initiator.startHook();
411:       try {
412:         // Await admission rather than pipeline: its rejection must skip this occurrence before the
413:         // callback attempt is counted or either returned capability is used.
414:         // @ts-expect-error Worker RPC's mapped return type wraps the already-stubbed hook result.
415:         hookResult = await hookCall;
416:       } catch {
417:         this.#rejectPending(prepared, Date.now());
418:         return true;
419:       }
420: 
421:       const admitted = this.#markAdmitted(prepared, Date.now());
422:       if (!admitted || !hookResult) return false;
423: 
424:       const firing: ScheduledFiring = {
425:         scheduleId: prepared.scheduleId,
426:         runId: prepared.runId,
427:         scheduledTime: prepared.scheduledTime,
428:         actualTime: Date.now(),
429:         timeZone: timeZoneOf(admitted.state),
430:       };
431:       try {
432:         await hookResult.approvalQueue.authorizeObservation({
433:           title: `Run scheduled task: ${admitted.title}`,
434:           description: `Deliver scheduled task ${prepared.scheduleId} for its planned occurrence at ${prepared.scheduledTime}.`,
435:         });
436:       } catch {
437:         this.#failPending(prepared, "authorization_failed", Date.now());
438:         return false;
439:       }
440: 
441:       if (!this.#isPendingDelivery(prepared)) return false;
442:       try {
443:         await hookResult.callback.onSchedule(firing);
444:       } catch {
445:         this.#failPending(prepared, "callback_failed", Date.now());
446:         return false;
447:       }
448:       this.#completePending(prepared, Date.now());
449:       return false;
450:     } finally {
451:       disposeStub(capabilities.initiator);
452:     }
453:   }

455:   async #deliverSafely(key: string, schedule: StoredSchedule): Promise<boolean> {
456:     const { workspaceId, scheduleId } = schedule.state;
457:     return obsContext.with({ workspaceId, scheduleId }, async () => {
458:       try {
459:         return await this.#deliver(key);

461:         this.#reportDeliveryFailure(error);

463:       }
464:     });

478:   #prepareRun(key: string, now: number): PreparedRun | undefined {
479:     return this.ctx.storage.transactionSync(() => {
480:       this.#requireLiveMetadata();
481:       const stored = this.#readSchedule(key);
482:       if (!stored || !isDue(stored, now)) return undefined;
483: 
484:       let state = stored.state;
485:       if (state.status === "pending" && state.stage === "delivery") {
486:         state = failRun(state, state.runId, "callback_failed", now);
487:         this.ctx.storage.kv.put<StoredSchedule>(key, { ...stored, state });
488:         return undefined;
489:       }
490:       const leaseExpiresAt = checkedAdd(now, RECOVERY_DELAY_MS);
491:       if (state.status === "active" || state.status === "retrying") {
492:         state = beginDueRun(state, now, crypto.randomUUID(), leaseExpiresAt);
493:       } else if (state.status === "pending") {
494:         state = { ...state, leaseExpiresAt };
495:       }
496:       if (state.status !== "pending") return undefined;
497:       this.ctx.storage.kv.put<StoredSchedule>(key, { ...stored, state });
498:       return {
499:         workspaceId: state.workspaceId,
500:         scheduleId: state.scheduleId,
501:         runId: state.runId,
502:         scheduledTime: state.scheduledTime,
503:       };
504:     });
505:   }
506: 
507:   #markAdmitted(prepared: PreparedRun, now: number): StoredSchedule | undefined {
508:     return this.ctx.storage.transactionSync(() => {
509:       if (this.#requireMetadata().revoked) return undefined;
510:       const key = scheduleKey(prepared.workspaceId, prepared.scheduleId);
511:       const stored = this.#readSchedule(key);
512:       if (!matchesPending(stored, prepared)) return undefined;
513:       const leaseExpiresAt = checkedAdd(now, RECOVERY_DELAY_MS);
514:       const state =
515:         stored.state.stage === "admission"
516:           ? admitRun(stored.state, prepared.runId, now, leaseExpiresAt)
517:           : { ...stored.state, leaseExpiresAt };
518:       if (state.status !== "pending" || state.stage !== "delivery") return undefined;
519:       const admitted = { ...stored, state };
520:       this.ctx.storage.kv.put(key, admitted);
521:       return admitted;
522:     });
523:   }
524: 
525:   #rejectPending(prepared: PreparedRun, rejectedAt: number): void {
526:     this.#settle(prepared, undefined, (state) => rejectRun(state, prepared.runId, rejectedAt));
527:   }
528: 
529:   #failPending(
530:     prepared: PreparedRun,
531:     failureCode: "authorization_failed" | "callback_failed",
532:     failedAt: number,
533:   ): void {
534:     this.#settle(prepared, "delivery", (state) =>
535:       failRun(state, prepared.runId, failureCode, failedAt));
536:   }
537: 
538:   #completePending(prepared: PreparedRun, completedAt: number): void {
539:     this.#settle(prepared, "delivery", (state) =>
540:       completeRun(state, prepared.runId, completedAt));
541:   }
542: 
543:   #isPendingDelivery(prepared: PreparedRun): boolean {
544:     if (this.#requireMetadata().revoked) return false;
545:     const stored = this.#readSchedule(scheduleKey(prepared.workspaceId, prepared.scheduleId));
546:     return matchesPending(stored, prepared) && stored.state.stage === "delivery";
547:   }

549:   async #planAlarm(): Promise<void> {
550:     const metadata = this.#requireMetadata();
551:     if (metadata.revoked) {
552:       await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now());
553:       return;
554:     }
555:     let target: number | undefined;
556:     for (const [, schedule] of this.#listSchedules()) {
557:       const candidate = alarmTarget(schedule);
558:       if (candidate !== undefined && (target === undefined || candidate < target))
559:         target = candidate;
560:     }
561:     if (target === undefined) await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();
562:     else await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(target);
563:   }
564: 
565:   async #cleanupRevokedAccount(): Promise<void> {
566:     const entries = [...this.ctx.storage.kv.list({ limit: REVOCATION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE + 1 })];
567:     const cleanup = entries
568:       .filter(([key]) => key !== METADATA_KEY)
569:       .slice(0, REVOCATION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE);
570:     for (const [key, value] of cleanup) {
571:       if (key.startsWith(CAPABILITIES_PREFIX)) disposeCapabilities(value as StoredCapabilities);
572:     }
573:     this.ctx.storage.transactionSync(() => {
574:       for (const [key] of cleanup) this.ctx.storage.kv.delete(key);
575:     });
576:     const remains = [...this.ctx.storage.kv.list({ limit: 2 })].some(
577:       ([key]) => key !== METADATA_KEY,
578:     );
579:     if (remains) await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now());
580:     else await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();
581:   }

583:   #readSchedule(key: string): StoredSchedule | undefined {
584:     const value = this.ctx.storage.kv.get<unknown>(key);
585:     return value === undefined ? undefined : decodeStoredSchedule(key, value, "reject");
586:   }
587: 
588:   #listSchedules(prefix = SCHEDULE_PREFIX, limit?: number): Array<[string, StoredSchedule]> {
589:     const schedules: Array<[string, StoredSchedule]> = [];
590:     for (const [key, value] of this.ctx.storage.kv.list<unknown>({ prefix, limit })) {
591:       const schedule = decodeStoredSchedule(key, value, "skip");
592:       if (schedule) schedules.push([key, schedule]);
593:     }
594:     return schedules;
595:   }
596: 
597:   #requireMetadata(): DriverMetadata {
598:     const metadata = this.ctx.storage.kv.get<DriverMetadata>(METADATA_KEY);
599:     if (metadata === undefined) return { schemaVersion: 1, revoked: false };
600:     if (metadata.schemaVersion !== 1 || typeof metadata.revoked !== "boolean") {
601:       throw new Error("Unsupported scheduler driver metadata.");
602:     }
603:     return metadata;
604:   }
605: 
606:   #requireLiveMetadata(initialize = false): DriverMetadata {
607:     const metadata = this.#requireMetadata();
608:     if (metadata.revoked) throw new Error("Scheduler account is permanently revoked.");
609:     if (initialize && this.ctx.storage.kv.get(METADATA_KEY) === undefined) {
610:       this.ctx.storage.kv.put<DriverMetadata>(METADATA_KEY, metadata);
611:     }
612:     return metadata;
613:   }
614: }

616: function decodeStoredSchedule(
617:   key: string,
618:   value: unknown,
619:   mode: "reject" | "skip",
620: ): StoredSchedule | undefined {
621:   if (typeof value === "object" && value !== null && "version" in value && value.version === 1) {
622:     return value as StoredSchedule;
623:   }
624: 
625:   const error = new Error(`Unsupported scheduler schedule row: ${key}`);
626:   logger.error("unsupported scheduler schedule row", {
627:     event: "scheduler.schedule-row.unsupported",
628:     error,
629:   });
630:   reportIssue("scheduler.schedule-row.unsupported", error, {
631:     handled: true,
632:     attributes: obsContext.get(),
633:   });
634:   if (mode === "reject") throw error;
635:   return undefined;
636: }
637: 
638: function matchesPending(
639:   stored: StoredSchedule | undefined,
640:   prepared: PreparedRun,
641: ): stored is StoredSchedule & { state: Extract<EnabledSchedule, { status: "pending" }> } {
642:   return stored?.state.status === "pending" && stored.state.runId === prepared.runId;
643: }
644: 
645: function isDue(schedule: StoredSchedule, now: number): boolean {
646:   const state = schedule.state;
647:   if (state.status === "active") return state.nextFire <= now;
648:   if (state.status === "retrying") return state.nextAttempt <= now;
649:   if (state.status === "pending") return state.leaseExpiresAt <= now;
650:   return false;
651: }
652: 
653: /** True once a schedule can never fire again, so its stored capability is dead weight. */
654: function isTerminal(state: EnabledSchedule): boolean {
655:   return state.status === "completed" || state.status === "expired" || state.status === "dead";
656: }
657: 
658: function alarmTarget(schedule: StoredSchedule): number | undefined {
659:   const state = schedule.state;
660:   if (state.status === "active") return state.nextFire;
661:   if (state.status === "retrying") return state.nextAttempt;
662:   if (state.status === "pending") return state.leaseExpiresAt;
663:   return undefined;
664: }
665: 
666: function timeZoneOf(state: EnabledSchedule): string {
667:   return state.spec.kind === "interval" ? "UTC" : state.spec.timeZone;
668: }
669: 
670: function toScheduleSummary(schedule: StoredSchedule): ScheduleSummary {
671:   const common = {
672:     scheduleId: schedule.state.scheduleId,
673:     title: schedule.title,
674:     description: schedule.description,
675:     cadence: toScheduleCadence(schedule.state.spec),
676:     occurrences: schedule.state.occurrences,
677:     occurrenceCount: schedule.state.occurrences ? schedule.state.occurrenceCount ?? 0 : undefined,
678:   };
679:   const state = schedule.state;
680:   switch (state.status) {
681:     case "active":
682:       return { ...common, status: "active", nextFire: state.nextFire };
683:     case "pending":
684:       return { ...common, status: "active", nextFire: state.nextFire ?? state.scheduledTime };
685:     case "retrying":
686:       return { ...common, status: "active", nextFire: state.nextAttempt, retrying: true };
687:     case "dead":
688:       return {
689:         ...common,
690:         status: "dead",
691:         failedAt: state.failedAt,
692:         failureCode: state.failureCode,
693:       };
694:     case "completed":
695:       return { ...common, status: "completed", completedAt: state.completedAt };
696:     case "expired":
697:       return { ...common, status: "expired", expiredAt: state.expiredAt };
698:   }
699: }
700: 
701: function compareScheduleSummaries(left: ScheduleSummary, right: ScheduleSummary): number {
702:   const leftTime =
703:     left.status === "active" ? (left.nextFire ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) : terminalTime(left);
704:   const rightTime =
705:     right.status === "active" ? (right.nextFire ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) : terminalTime(right);
706:   return leftTime - rightTime || left.scheduleId.localeCompare(right.scheduleId);
707: }
708: 
709: function terminalTime(summary: Exclude<ScheduleSummary, { status: "active" }>): number {
710:   if (summary.status === "dead") return summary.failedAt;
711:   if (summary.status === "completed") return summary.completedAt;
712:   return summary.expiredAt;
713: }
714: 
715: function compareDueSchedules(
716:   [leftKey, left]: [string, StoredSchedule],
717:   [rightKey, right]: [string, StoredSchedule],
718: ): number {
719:   return alarmTarget(left)! - alarmTarget(right)! || leftKey.localeCompare(rightKey);
720: }

722: async function runBounded<T>(
723:   values: readonly T[],
724:   concurrency: number,
725:   run: (value: T) => Promise<void>,
726: ): Promise<void> {

3: // This module owns all manipulation of the `collaborators` and `shareKeys` storage collections
4: // and the permission graph that links them. It deliberately performs no RPC: anything that

6: // profile, notifying a user that a gadget was opened, etc.) stays in the Overseer, which passes
7: // resolved values (or, where laziness matters, a callback) into this module.
8: //
9: // LAZY REVOCATION MODEL: Access is determined by reachability from the owner in the permission
10: // graph, recomputed live at every open() (see `getEffectiveRole`). Revocation is therefore lazy:
11: // removing a collaborator only severs the edges granting *them* access, and revoking a share link
12: // only flags the link revoked. Nothing cascades, no records are deleted, and downstream edges are
13: // never touched -- users who lose their only path to the owner simply become unreachable and are
14: // denied at open() time. Because the graph is never destructively pruned, revocation is reversible:
15: // re-adding a removed collaborator restores them and, transitively, everyone they had shared with.
16: // (Records and revoked keys accumulate in storage; a future GC could reclaim long-dead entries.)
